en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Couplet on Accompanied by Vitakka (Savitakkaduka)
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, accompanied by applied thought (*savitakka*), there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive,
and not accompanied by applied thought, by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*). Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, accompanied by applied thought,

there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor reactive, and not accompanied by applied thought, by way of root-condition …pe… dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable and non-reactive, accompanied by applied thought … [and so forth].

Dependent on states that are non-demonstrable and non-reactive, and not accompanied by applied thought, there arise states that are non-demonstrable and non-reactive, and not accompanied by applied thought, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
There are six [conditions] in the case of roots, three in the case of objects, and so forth... six in the case of non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and without applied thought, there arises a state that is not non-demonstrable and non-reactive, and not without applied thought, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and without applied thought, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable and non-reactive nor without applied thought, by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and without applied thought...
States that are non-apparent, non-reactive, and without applied thought, as well as those that are non-apparent, non-reactive, and without applied thought, arise by way of the root condition.
(Abbreviated. There are three [answers] for the root condition … pe … three for the non-disappearance condition.
